correctness.rationale: Oddness is preserved by this Fourier convention. Each support has an even cardinality, 2a and 2b, and Parseval plus Cauchy–Schwarz gives 4ab>=27. Hence a+b>=6. At equality, odd Fourier inversion sends any support-size split to the reversed split, since the square of the transform is 27 times reflection, or -27 times identity on odd functions. This justifies the source's symmetry shorthand; matrix transpose alone is not the argument. I independently enumerated the restricted sine-matrix ranks over F_271 using z=5, a root of order 27 (z^9=28 is a nontrivial cube root), with incremental row elimination. The 16731, 55770 and 81796 patterns for (1,5), (2,4), (3,3) have just one exception: both pair-index sets {3,6,12}, with rank 2. The specialization is lawful algebraically because Phi_27(z)=1+z^9+z^18=0; each nonzero reduced minor certifies a nonzero complex minor. At the exception, a difference of order-three characters on 3G gives a complex null vector by the orthogonality sum on Z/9: its Fourier support is y=±3 mod 9, and its time support consists of 3u with u nonzero mod 3. Each is the stated six-point set. The rank lower bound and this witness give a one-dimensional complex kernel, with no inference from modular singularity alone.
residual_risks: The finite exact certificate applies only to equality at cyclic order 27 and the asserted complex odd subspace. It does not give a quantitative stability claim or a prime-cube family classification.

originality.rationale: Credit is limited to the complete projective equality classification, not the numerical sum lower bound or the construction alone. The inspected inequalities and exact results on other groups do not classify this odd slice on the cyclic prime cube. Delvaux–Van Barel is a material remaining coverage risk: the available descriptions do not establish that its rank-block results at prime powers imply these exact odd coefficient lines. This best-of-knowledge assessment makes no priority claim.
residual_risks: The prime-power submatrix paper was not read in full; a genuinely implying theorem there or elsewhere cannot be excluded. The related order-25 case mentioned without a citation was not identified. Focused index and literature searches cannot prove global novelty.

value.rationale: This resolves the equality geometry of a natural odd Fourier uncertainty problem on the smallest cyclic odd prime cube. The scalar uniqueness and exact support locations distinguish the possible extremizers from what the numerical bounds and known general composite-order obstructions can tell a researcher. It is a complete classification, not a support-size table, and the finite rank step answers a precise motivated question.
residual_risks: No broad generalization in the prime or quantitative stability is claimed.
